title: Investigating psychological and neural correlates of intimate partner violence
summary: Close relationships hold great potential but often also the risk of conflicts resulting in aggression. The detailed understanding of conflict dynamics leading to aggression and their influencing individual factors in cognitive and behavioral processes remain to be explored. We focus on the investigation of precursors and dynamics of conflict escalation and appraisal (blame attribution) between siblings and non-siblings varying in cognitive control capacity during fMRI hyperscanning. Additionally, social interaction between healthy strangers is investigated as control group (arm 3). Main research questions of the project are: How do cognitive control deficits of one person affect conflict dynamics and aggression (i.e.; at what time does loss of control lead to conflict?) in close relationships? (objective 1), What are neurocognitive patterns during conflict formation in close relationships? (objective 2), Are there biosignature-specific neural and behavioral patterns of developing or de-escalating conflicts in close relationships? (objective 3). Long-term aim is the investigation of neural changes and aggressive interactions in dyads after improvement of cognitive control. The study investigates how deficits in self-regulation influence conflict behavior in close relationships. On the one hand, groups of people with a mental disorder and a sibling and, on the other hand, groups of people with a mental disorder and strangers are examined. The aim is to identify neurocognitive patterns in the escalation and de-escalation of conflicts and aggressive behavior and to understand how these are influenced by the participants' self-regulation.
conditions: All kinds of mental disorders according to DSM-5/ICD-11 except dementias, i.e. including substance use disorders, psychotic disorders, affective disorders, anxiety disorders, PTSD, ASPD, BPD, CD, ODD, ADHD, ASD

interventions.name:
Patient-Sibling Pairs

80 people will be included, divided into 40 pairs. There will be 40 patients with a mental disorder and one sibling each.

All participants will be between the ages of 18 and 40.

The study will include patients suffering from all types of mental disorders according to D

Patient-Stranger Pairs

80 people will be included, divided into 40 pairs. The same 40 patients who participated in arm 1 will be included, as well as a control (stranger).

All participants will be between the ages of 18 and 40.

The study will include patients suffering from all types of men

Control-Control Pairs

80 healthy control people will be included, divided into 40 pairs.  All participants will be between the ages of 18 and 40. Participants are screened for the presence of psychiatric diseases via the Mini-Dips questionnaire.

Participants with acute or chronic mental health

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Undoubted understanding of the study information
Voluntary signing of the informed consent form
Patient group: persons with mental disorders according to the DSM-5/ICD-11 criteria, including substance use disorders, psychoses, affective disorders, anxiety disorders, PTSD, ASPD, BPD, CD, ODD, ADHD, ASD 
Siblings: age difference not more than 5 years
Exclusion criteria:
Significant cognitive limitations language problems that interfere with understanding the study procedure. Inability to comply with the study protocol severe somatic or neurological diseases such as encephalitis or hormonal tumors or dementia 
MRI-specific exclusion criteria: Claustrophobia and contraindications (e.g. metal implants)
